overall: Explainer register, steady and clear, a person who knows rural medicine telling you what the delay costs. The read builds through the chain of delays, drops to its quietest on the wait statistic and the stakes, lifts once for the tool, and lands lower and more certain than its middle.

lines.text: A crash patient rolls into the nearest ER, and often there's no trauma surgeon on call. Often it's a Level Four center, a well equipped rural emergency room.
lines.intent: Cold open on the scene, plain and concrete.
lines.note: Weight on 'no trauma surgeon'. Matter of fact, with the well equipped rural room named without fuss.

lines.text: The doctor there treats everything from strokes to pediatric flu. Trauma is rarely her strength, because these towns don't see a lot of injury.
lines.intent: Name the doctor's real limit and why it is not her fault.
lines.note: Emphasis on 'rarely'. Slightly dry, no apology.

lines.text: First she has to decide to transfer. That decision alone takes 15 to 30 minutes today.
lines.intent: Open the first delay, the decision to transfer.
lines.note: Emphasis on 'decision'. Land '15 to 30 minutes' flat, no lift.

lines.text: Texas has 173 basic Level Four centers, and only 22 at Level One.
lines.intent: Give the scale of the gap between centers.
lines.note: Emphasis on 'only'. Read both numbers plainly.

lines.text: Then she has to hospital shop by phone for a trauma center that will take the patient, and call an ambulance.
lines.intent: Stack the second and third delays, the phone search and the ambulance.
lines.note: Emphasis on 'by phone'. Slight forward push, a person listing chores.

lines.text: After the yes comes the wait. State registry data show up to 80 percent of the most severely injured wait more than two hours to be transferred.
lines.intent: Deliver the central statistic on the wait.
lines.note: Emphasis on 'two hours'. The quietest and most certain line of the first half. Land 'up to 80 percent' without stress.

lines.text: The stakes are high. Trauma is the leading cause of death for people up to age 45.
lines.intent: State the stakes without raising the voice.
lines.note: Emphasis on 'leading cause of death'. Steady, a fact being stated.

lines.text: In San Antonio, trauma surgeon Brian Eastridge spent much of his career as an Army trauma surgeon in war zones. Now he co-leads iRemedyACT, a statewide team using AI on this delay.
lines.intent: Introduce the person and the tool.
lines.note: Emphasis on 'war zones'. Say Eastridge as EAST-ridge and iRemedyACT as eye-REM-eh-dee act, naturally.

lines.text: Their tool flags signs of severe injury and prompts an earlier transfer call. It pushes the doctor to make that decision sooner.
lines.intent: Explain what the tool does in plain terms.

lines.text: With the tool, that decision could take five to 10 minutes.
lines.intent: Show the payoff of the tool, scaled to the earlier delay.
lines.note: Emphasis on 'five to 10 minutes'. The one lift of hope, still restrained.

lines.text: A faster decision still leaves the calls and the ride. A survival benefit is something he suspects.
lines.note: Emphasis on 'suspects'. Drop the energy, candid and measured.

lines.text: He calls it just a tool, like an ultrasound. It sharpens the doctor's judgment instead of replacing it.
lines.intent: Give his own framing, humble and grounded.
lines.note: Emphasis on 'instead of replacing'. Dry, a doctor's modesty.

lines.text: A UT System AI moonshot called BEACON plans to test an AI assistant at seven UT hospital sites. As of September, a statewide pilot of the transfer tool was planned for the fall.
lines.intent: Report the status of the rollout accurately.
lines.note: Emphasis on 'planned'. Say BEACON as BEE-kon. Informational, no promise.

lines.text: The call could come sooner. The road is still the road.
lines.intent: Close low and certain, the line the film is built toward.
lines.note: Emphasis on 'still the road'. Lower than the middle of the film, final and unhurried.
